annotations.title: Get a verification receipt by proof code

description:
Give back the Fuentio receipt of a verification by its proof code: outcome and reasons, status, legal form, registered office, insolvency (what was searched), source, check time, hash and the public link to check it.
Use it when the user asks for a receipt or proof of a check. Always ask the user first: 'Normal or detailed receipt?', then call it. Use the proof code from verify_company. Don't use it to run a new check: call verify_company.
Inputs: proof_code (e.g. 'FUE-FR-20261015-DZ7TP9', any case; a lookup's meta.receipt.request_id also works, same key), format 'normal' or 'detailed'.
Returns: data.markdown, the branded receipt: show it as is; data.text, plain text.
Limits: free; 30 a minute. The key that ran the check also sees its reference; anyone else, the public view. Read-only.

format.description: Ask the user first: 'normal' (the receipt) or 'detailed' (also every check, the signals, changes, sources and the full hash re-checked).
format.title: Format

proof_code.description: The proof code verify_company returned (FUE-XX-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX; any case or spacing), or a lookup's meta.receipt.request_id.
proof_code.title: Proof Code

name: get_receipt

outputSchema.description:
get_receipt (brief 009): the Fuentio receipt by proof code. `data.markdown` is the
branded receipt to show as is, `data.text` the same in plain text; the rest is the JSON
(`kind`, `format`, `proof_code`, `header`, `outcome`, `status`, `legal_form`,
`registered_office`, `insolvency`, `source`, `checked_at`, `hash`, `check_url`).
Detailed adds `checks`, `signals`, `changes_summary`, `sources`, `data_sha256`,
`unchanged`, `served_at` and `limits`. A lookup's request id gives that lookup's proof
(`kind: lookup_receipt`).
outputSchema.title: ReceiptOutput
